rows: Win32_Process exposes CommandLine, ExecutablePath, ProcessId, ParentProcessId and CreationDate.
A command-line substring alone is not a complete process identity.
Windows Job Objects can manage groups of processes and support terminating all associated processes.
Processes must be assigned and the job handle lifecycle must be controlled.
TerminateJobObject terminates all processes associated with a job object.
Required access rights and assignment must be established before timeout handling.
Wait-Process waits for the identified process; Microsoft notes Start-Process -Wait covers a process tree while Wait-Process waits only for identified processes.
Waiting or stopping one PID does not prove descendant cleanup.
Get-Process returns local process objects and detailed process information.
PID reuse requires start-time and executable identity checks.
Start-Process creates a local process and can return a process object with PassThru.
The returned parent process object alone does not authenticate later descendants.
Flush(true) writes buffered data through intermediate file buffers.
A flush does not by itself provide schema validation or multi-file transaction identity.
File.Replace replaces one file with another and can preserve a backup.
Generation manifests and same-volume policy remain separate.
The API returns the final normalized path for an opened file handle.
The file must be opened under the intended reparse and sharing policy.
Windows distinguishes process handles and process identifiers; identifiers can be reused after process termination.
PID-only receipts are insufficient for durable process identity.
Set-Content creates or replaces file content and also supports alternate data streams on Windows.
Direct Set-Content is not a durable atomic receipt protocol.
git push supports atomic ref updates and explicit force-with-lease expectations.
An expected remote value must be pinned for authoritative optimistic concurrency.
git fetch downloads objects and updates remote-tracking refs according to the configured remote and refspec.
The named remote URL and fetched ref identity must be verified.
git remote manages named remotes and can report configured fetch and push URLs.
A remote name alone does not prove canonical repository identity.
git merge supports --ff-only to refuse non-fast-forward integration.
Fast-forward safety still depends on the correct remote and branch identity.
git stash push can include untracked files and creates stash commits referenced through refs/stash.
The current refs/stash value must be distinguished from a pre-existing stash.
git hash-object computes the repository object ID for exact file bytes.
The repository object format and TOCTOU between hashing and execution remain relevant.
git rev-parse resolves revisions and repository information.
A resolved local ref is not automatically a fresh remote readback.
Python JSON decoding exposes object_pairs_hook and parse_constant for stricter application policies.
Default decoding does not reject every ambiguous control payload.
Python documents flushing a buffered file before os.fsync to push buffered data to storage.
Directory-entry and multi-file durability need additional policy.
Updating a repository file requires the blob SHA being replaced; concurrent content changes can conflict.
Sequential optimistic updates and post-write readback are still required.
The current INSPIRE package was published on 5 July 2026 and is replaced on the first Sunday monthly.
Catalogue availability does not prove the exact downloaded GML bytes.
The official DTM source is 1 m, EPSG:27700, metres ODN and approximately ±0.15 m RMSE.
Fresh WCS bytes and polygon samples remain unobserved in this support runtime.
Terrain 50 grid supply uses 200 by 200 cells, 50 m spacing and 10 km tiles.
The exact current archive and sidecar hashes remain required.
